fields.mechanism: Biofilm formation on catheter surfaces that promotes infection and thrombus development.
fields.intervention: Embed a low‑frequency ultrasonic transducer within the catheter wall to emit acoustic waves that, together with the dialysis fluid shear, disrupt and prevent biofilm accumulation while preserving the antithrombotic luminal coating.
fields.expected_effect: Reduced biofilm buildup and associated heparin‑binding thrombus formation, maintaining catheter patency and coating biocompatibility.
fields.falsification_test: In an in‑vitro dialysis flow loop, compare coated catheters with and without ultrasonic activation; measure biofilm mass (e.g., crystal violet staining) and thrombus formation under identical shear conditions—no significant reduction would falsify the proposed mechanism.
